response: Yes, financial incentives have been shown to be a cost-effective strategy to support smoking cessation during pregnancy. Studies have found that offering financial incentives, such as vouchers or cash rewards, to pregnant women who quit smoking can be a cost-effective way to improve quit rates and reduce the risks associated with smoking during pregnancy. These incentives can be particularly effective when combined with other evidence-based cessation strategies, such as counseling and medication. By helping women quit smoking, financial incentives can also reduce healthcare costs associated with smoking-related complications during pregnancy and childbirth.
